surfaces.title: useSession(selector) read hook
surfaces.current: const { useSession, t } = props; useSession(s => s.running) etc. (4 call sites)
surfaces.postMigration: Slot runtime props expose the new snapshot hook (symbol name per card) plus a separate stream hook: useSnapshot(s => s.state.busy), useSnapshot(s => s.state.activeCalls.length > 0), useSnapshot(s => s.turns.at(-1)?.endReason), useStream(stream => isThinking(stream.partial?.blocks ?? [])).
surfaces.note: If shipped untyped, the destructured useSession is undefined and the first call throws TypeError on the first render: the pet never appears at all.

surfaces.title: snapshot.running lifecycle flag
surfaces.current: const running = useSession(s => s.running)  // discarded at :26 via void running
surfaces.postMigration: Native: useSnapshot(s => s.state.busy). Deferred: useSnapshot(s => s.compat.running) (or root alias s.running; placement unconfirmed U-3).
surfaces.note: Silent break: a missing property yields undefined rather than throwing; the read is currently dead code.

surfaces.title: snapshot.runningCalls in-flight calls
surfaces.postMigration: Native: useSnapshot(s => s.state.activeCalls.length > 0). Deferred: useSnapshot(s => s.compat.runningCalls.length > 0) - the projection keeps the array shape, not just a count.
surfaces.note: Largest blast radius of the four selectors: a dereference on a missing field throws inside the selector during render and can take the whole header down.

surfaces.title: snapshot.turnEnds[].reason turn history
surfaces.postMigration: const lastTurnEnd = useSnapshot(s => s.turns.at(-1)?.endReason); then remap the vocabulary explicitly (e.g. lastTurnEnd === 'completed').
surfaces.note: Optional chaining is on the element, not the array access, so s.turnEnds.length throws. Separately the end-reason VALUE domain changed: a rename-only migration compiles and then silently never matches - a wrong-pose bug with no error.

surfaces.title: snapshot.partial.blocks streaming reasoning detection
surfaces.current: function isThinking(snapshot: ConversationSnapshot) { return snapshot.partial?.blocks.some(block => block.kind === 'reasoning') ?? false } ; const thinking = useSession(isThinking)
surfaces.postMigration: function isThinking(blocks: readonly ContentBlock[]) { return blocks.some(block => block.kind === 'thinking') } ; const thinking = useStream(stream => isThinking(stream.partial?.blocks ?? []))
surfaces.note: Null-safe expression: when the field disappears it quietly returns false instead of throwing, so the pet silently sits in the idle frame for a whole model turn. The block discriminant also changed. isThinking can no longer be a snapshot selector - it must become a stream selector.

rule: A field may ride the compatibility projection only if it is (1) derivable from the new state model with no second source of truth, (2) its VALUE DOMAIN is unchanged (a renamed field is fine, a renamed value is not), and (3) it lives on the same channel as the new snapshot.
Criterion 2 is the trap: a projection that restores a field NAME but not its VALUE VOCABULARY turns a loud break into a silent wrong answer.

mustSwitchImmediately.reason: Value domain changed - a same-named alias would silently never match, so the settled-turn frame never fires.
Different channel (streaming content is not part of the snapshot projection) AND the block discriminant changed; the null-safe expression silently returns false.

sequencing: Release N (the 0.1.2-alpha.2 bump): hook rename (S2) + native read paths for S5 and S6 + projection reads for S3 and S4.
Release N+1 (after the projection window closes): move to state.busy / state.activeCalls and drop the projection dependency, tracked against card DSH-0.1.2-A1-06.
If the projection is off by default in the host config, S3/S4 are immediate switches too - the projection is a host-side feature and must not be assumed (U-5).
